Schematic diagram demonstrating menaquinone-7 (MK-7) restores mitochondrial function and determines the fate of bone marrow mesenchymal stem cells (BMSCs) via mitophagy pathways. Upon the binding of MK-7 to its nuclear receptor pregnane X receptor (PXR), the extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1/2 (ERK1/2)/cyclic AMP-responsive element-binding protein (CREB) pathway is activated, leading to an elevation expression in cellular communication network factor 2 (Ccn2). Subsequently, the Ccn2 drives PTEN- induced kinase 1 (PINK1)-dependent mitophagy, which eliminates mitochondrial DNA (mtDNA) and mitigates mitochondrial reactive oxygen species (mtROS). Thereby, cellular senescence is reversed and osteogenic differentiation in primary BMSCs of aged bones is enhanced. The schematic diagram was created by BioRender.com. ATP: adenosine triphosphate; LC3: microtubule-associated protein 1 light chain 3; MMP: mitochondrial membrane potential; p-CREB: phosphorylated cAMP response element binding protein; p-ERK1/2: phosphorylated extracellular signal-regulated kinases 1/2; SASP: senescence-associated secretory phenotype.
